description: We are Team CodeCraft IT, a group of driven engineers, and innovators united by our passion for space exploration, aerospace technology, and high-performance software engineering. Our shared vision of making real astrophysics accessible and engaging brought us together to tackle this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge with our Planetary Defense Simulator.
summary:
NASA DART Planetary Defense Simulator by CodeCraft IT is an interactive orbital physics and engineering platform that empowers users to design, simulate, and execute kinetic impact missions to divert hazardous Near-Earth Asteroids (NEOs). Built upon verified datasets from NASA JPL CNEOS and Nature 616 (2023) research, the simulator challenges players across four realistic threat tiers: from baseline target (65803) Dimorphos, to hazardous rubble-piles Apophis and Bennu, up to high-priority threat 2024 YR4 (Torino Level 3 record).

Users act as a NASA Flight Director: assembling kinetic impactors while balancing rocket propulsion, payload mass, mission budgets, and Delta-V constraints. The system models realistic aerospace factors, including atmospheric Max-Q stress, solar panel deployment, and the 76-second speed-of-light Deep Space Network delay at 11M km, requiring autonomous SMART Nav optical lock.

Upon hypervelocity intercept (up to 38 km/s), the simulation computes kinetic momentum transfer, factoring in asteroid ejecta recoil (

details:
NASA DART Planetary Defense Simulator

Team: CodeCraft IT

1. What Does It Do or How Does It Work?

The NASA DART Planetary Defense Simulator is an interactive, browser-based aerospace engineering and orbital physics simulation that models humanity's primary technique for asteroid mitigation: hypervelocity kinetic impact deflection.

The application guides users through a comprehensive three-stage mission lifecycle:

  1. Target Threat Selection & Intelligence Briefing:
    Players choose from four calibrated threat levels based on verified NASA JPL CNEOS catalogs:
    • Level 1 (Verified Baseline): (65803) Dimorphos — the real target of NASA's historic 2022 DART mission.
    • Level 2 (High-Risk Approach): (99942) Apophis — monitored by NASA OSIRIS-APEX for its close 31,600 km Earth passage.
    • Level 3 (Extinction-Scale Rubble Pile): (101955) Bennu — carbonaceous asteroid mapped by NASA OSIRIS-REx.
    • Level 4 (Emergency Sentry Alert): 2024 YR4 — the newly discovered asteroid that reached an unprecedented Level 3 on the Torino Scale in late 2024.
    • Launch Vehicles: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Space Launch System (SLS), and Starship Super Heavy.
    • Propulsion & Power: Chemical bipropellant vs. high-efficiency NEXT-C Xenon Ion thrusters (Isp=4,190 sI_{sp} = 4,190\text{ s}Isp​=4,190 s) paired with Roll-Out Solar Arrays (ROSA, 6.6 kW6.6\text{ kW}6.6 kW).
    • Autonomous Guidance & Optics: High-resolution DRACO optical camera and SMART Nav closed-loop tracking algorithms.
    • Secondary Payloads: LICIACube 6U CubeSat for ejecta plume photography.
    • Resource Budgets: Every choice impacts Total Launch Mass (<700 kg< 700\text{ kg}<700 kg), Mission Budget (<$450M< \$450\text{M}<$450M), and Required ΔV\Delta VΔV.
  2. 3D Atmospheric Ascent & Deep-Space Intercept:
    The simulator renders a multi-camera 3D flight sequence from Vandenberg SFB Space Launch Complex 4E through aerodynamic Max-Q, fairing separation, interplanetary cruise, and terminal optical intercept.
  3. Kinetic Deflection Verification & Incident Review:
    Upon intercept (velocities between 6.14 km/s6.14\text{ km/s}6.14 km/s and 38.4 km/s38.4\text{ km/s}38.4 km/s), the engine calculates kinetic energy delivered (EkE_kEk​), momentum transfer, and orbital deflection offset (Δv\Delta vΔv). If an engineering parameter fails, an Incident Review Board generates a root-cause forensic breakdown.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Bridging Complex Astrophysics and Public Intuition: Translates complex orbital mechanics, hypervelocity physics, and Palermo/Torino hazard tables into accessible, visual, and interactive gameplay.
  • Realistic Aerospace Trade-offs: Teaches users that space exploration is about compromise—adding armor or heavier engines increases fuel requirements, pushes budget past statutory limits, and risks structural shear.
  • Immediate Feedback Loop: Rather than presenting static equations, the simulator demonstrates immediate consequences: inadequate fairing causes aerodynamic breakup at Max-Q; omitting autonomous SMART Nav causes a miss due to the speed-of-light communication lag.
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Requires no installation, runtimes, or downloads—runs smoothly on modern mobile and desktop browsers with dual-language support (English and Russian).

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Promoting Planetary Defense Literacy: Raises awareness for the vital work conducted by the NASA Planetary Defense Coordination Office (PDCO), Johns Hopkins APL, and the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN).
  • Inspiring the Next Generation of STEM Pioneers: Introduces students, educators, and space enthusiasts to real aerospace disciplines: telemetry analysis, payload integration, optical guidance, and orbital mechanics.
  • Demystifying Asteroid Threats: Replaces sci-fi sensationalism (such as "nuking an asteroid") with scientifically proven kinetic impact methods, demonstrating how a minute velocity offset of fractions of a millimeter per second (mm/s\text{mm/s}mm/s) diverts an asteroid millions of kilometers over astronomical timescales.

4. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Did You Use?

  • Frontend Framework: React 19 with Vite for ultra-fast compilation and optimized component rendering.
    • NASA JPL Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) Sentry Table.
    • NASA Small-Body Database Query Engine.
    • Peer-reviewed findings published in Nature 616, 2023 regarding the DART impact momentum enhancement factor (β\betaβ).
  • Presentation & Documentation: Python (python-pptx) for automated 7-slide NASA briefing decks, Git/GitHub for version control.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

  • Interactive Telemetry HUD (Heads-Up Display): Designed to look and feel like an authentic NASA mission control console, complete with dynamic g-force, aerodynamic pressure (QQQ), DSN link status, and skin temperature meters.
  • Procedural DRACO Camera Stream: Instead of relying on static video loops that can fail, we implemented a procedural HTML5 Canvas system that simulates actual optical navigation frames taken by the onboard DRACO telescope as it closes in on the asteroid at hypersonic speeds.
  • Dual Outcomes with Forensic Post-Mortem: Rather than a simple "Game Over" screen, mission failures trigger an Incident Review Board that conducts an educational root-cause analysis (e.g., explaining why light-speed delay prevented ground intervention).
  • Dynamic Ejecta Momentum Multiplier (β\betaβ): Models the counter-intuitive scientific reality that the debris ejected backward from an impact acts as a natural rocket thruster, magnifying momentum transfer up to 3.61×3.61\times3.61× beyond the mass of the probe itself.

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  1. Relativistic Communication Lag: Radio commands traveling at the speed of light take 76 seconds round-trip over a distance of 11 million kilometers. We factored this into the simulation to prove why terminal asteroid interception must be fully autonomous via onboard SMART Nav algorithms.
  2. Scientific Accuracy vs. Engagement: We ensured asteroid diameters, densities, orbital velocities, and masses match real NASA catalog data, while structuring the gameplay mechanics to remain engaging for non-technical users.
  3. Budget and Mass Constraints: Real space missions are bound by funding and rocket payload capacities. We introduced strict budget ceilings ($450M\$450\text{M}$450M) and launch mass limits to mirror actual NASA Discovery-class mission proposals.
  4. Accessibility and Global Reach: Implemented an instant language switcher between English and Russian, with fully localized technical terms, metric/imperial readouts, and responsive mobile-first UI controls.
  5. Fail-Safe Reliability: Engineered procedural graphic fallbacks for NASA video streams and optical feeds to ensure the web application never displays broken assets or empty screens during live demonstrations.
